Management Discussion and Analysis for the year 2017 
 
This report discusses the principal changes in the unaudited consolidated financial statements for the  year ended 
December 31, 2017. In June 2017, the Bank has combi ned National ITMX Co., Ltd to the Bank’s associate company 
in accordance with Thai Accounting Standard 28 (TAS  28): Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures.  The Bank 
considered its shareholding together with its power  to participate in the company’s operating policy t hrough its 
representatives in the position of the company’s board of directors as significant influence to the company. The Bank 
also restated the consolidated financial statements for Statements of Financial Position as at December 31, 2016 and 
Statements of Comprehensive Income for the year end ed December 31, 2016. However, the above change had  
insignificant impact to financial position and performance of the Bank. 
 
I. The Bank and Its Subsidiaries’ Overview for the year 2017  
 
In 2017, the Thai economy continued to expand due m ainly to exports and tourism sectors.  Merchandise exports 
continued to grow in all major export destinations and most product categories. Meanwhile, the tourism  sector 
expanded significantly due to increased foreign tourists especially Chinese and ASEAN tourists. However, the growth 
in the private investment sector remained relativel y low and concentrated only in a few business secto rs. In addition, 
the expansion of private consumption was suppressed  by the decreased in farm income during the second half of 
the year and the high household debt problem, which lowered purchasing power of low-income households.  
 
For the year 2017, KTB’s consolidated pre-provision  profit was Bt 73,746 m, decreased by Bt 312 m (0.4 2%). Fee 
and service income and operating expenses improved and offset the slight decrease in net interest inco me. In 
summary, the key changes of the Bank and its subsid iaries’ financial result compared to last year are as shown 
below: 
1) Net interest income declined by Bt 1,188 m (1.37 %) due mainly to the impact of the lending rate cut  on 
Minimum Retail Rate (MRR) at 0.50% in mid of May 20 17. Despite the mentioned impact on yield, the Bank  has 
continued to actively manage funding cost, resultin g in the slight decrease on Net Interest Margin (NI M) by 0.07% to 
3.23%, compared to 3.30% at the year 2016. 
2) Net fee and service income increased by Bt 1,979  (8.98%) as a result of the expansion of fee from ATM card 
business, electronic banking service fees and Banca ssurance. Meanwhile, KTB’s consolidated total other operating 
income decreased by Bt 2,327 m (14.84%) from the ye ar 2016 because of the lessening of net gain on tra ding and 
foreign exchange transactions as well as the decelerating of share of profit from investments on equit y method from 
the Bank’s associated company from insurance sector. 
3) Other operating expenses reduced by Bt 1,224 m ( 2.42%) as the Bank continues its cost management 
policy resulting in the slight reduction of the Cost-to-income compared to last year, from 40.61% to 40.12%. 
4) The Bank and its subsidiaries continue to mainta in a prudent coverage ratio. As at the end of Decem ber 
2017, coverage ratio was 121.71%. Provision expense s increased by Bt 11,404m (34.11%) from 2016, due t o the 
preparation to comply with IFRS9 standard.

2 
In 2017, The Bank and its subsidiaries’ net profit was Bt 24,116 m, showing a decline of Bt 9,450 m (28.15%) and the 
Net Profit Attributable to Equity Holders of the Bank was Bt 22,446 m, decreased by Bt 9,859 m (30.52%), mainly due 
to the increase of provision expense. 
 
The Bank’s consolidated total loan to customers (le ss deferred revenue) was Bt 1,938,082 m, rose by  
Bt 33,993 m (1.79%) from year 2016. The Bank focuse d on quality of loan growth as the loans to governm ent and 
state enterprise sector were well expanded. The Ban k’s consolidated deposits increased by Bt 98,471 m (4.99%) 
from saving and current deposits while time deposit s decreased as the Bank’s funding cost management p olicy and 
brought about loans to customers (less deferred revenue) -to-deposits ratio at 93.59%. 
 
The Bank’ consolidated NPLs as at December 31, 2017  was Bt 103,020 m, and gross NPLs ratio was 4.19% r ose 
from 3.97% as at December 31, 2016. The Bank has co ntinued to improve its strategies and business oper ating 
process emphasizing on quality of loan portfolio al ong with enhancing efficiency of monitoring and res tructuring 
process. The Bank will maintain its coverage ratio at the appropriate level. 
 
Overall, the Bank and its subsidiaries have strong financial position, solid capital level and effecti ve business 
operation to cope with any uncertainty in the future.

to Bt 44,833 m, increased by Bt 11,404 m (34.11%) compared to the year 2016. The bank set aside more provision to 
be a buffer for the increased NPLs, maintain its coverage ratio and prepare to comply with IFRS9 standard. Thus, the 
Banks and its subsidiaries’ coverage ratio was 121. 71% slightly changed from 121.57% as at December 31 , 2016 
and also increased from 115.37% as at September 30, 2017.  
 
In 2017 and 2016, the Banks wrote off NPLs in amount of Bt 23,739 m and Bt 1,509 m respectively.
